quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What happens to your field of vision when you drive faster?

options.text: It increases.
It decreases.
It makes it easier to see cross traffic.
It has no effect.

questions.correctAnswerText: It decreases.
questions.explanation: When you drive faster, your field of vision becomes smaller. You need to stay extra alert for hazards.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on wet roads?

options.text: As you drive faster, your tires grip the road less.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.
Slowing down makes the road more slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: As you drive faster, your tires grip the road less.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, faster speeds make your tires less effective. If you go too fast, your tires can lose grip and hydroplane, causing you to slide on water.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a main roadway from a private road?

options.text: Honk to warn other drivers.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert drivers.
Drive out fast to merge with traffic smoothly.
Let pedestrians and roadway traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians and roadway traffic go first.
questions.explanation: When entering a main roadway from a private road or driveway, you must let pedestrians and traffic on the roadway go first.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Hazard flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. Use fog lights if your vehicle has them. High beams bounce off fog and reduce your visibility.

questions.question: What does a good defensive driver do?

options.text: Drives slowly all the time.
Watches what other drivers do.
Travels at the same speed always.
Only drives in familiar areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches what other drivers do.
questions.explanation: A defensive driver watches other drivers and expects problems to happen. This helps prevent accidents.

questions.question: How can you stay out of a truck or bus driver's blind spot?

options.text: Never pass them.
Do not drive next to them or too close behind them.
Flash your lights at them.
Honk your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive next to them or too close behind them.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles like trucks and buses have big blind spots on the sides and rear. Stay away from these areas by not driving beside them or following too closely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Wildlife crossing.
School crossing or school zone.
Pedestrian crossing.
Business district.

questions.correctAnswerText: School crossing or school zone.
questions.explanation: Five-sided signs mean a school is nearby. Be alert for children and pedestrians. This sign warns of either a school crossing or school zone.

questions.question: What is true about drowsy drivers?

options.text: They should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
They can drive so poorly they look drunk.
Opening a window and turning up the radio keeps them alert.
Usually only older drivers get drowsy.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can drive so poorly they look drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive as poorly as drunk drivers. Coffee, open windows, or loud radio do not fix drowsiness.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
You must turn right.
Watch for traffic on your right.
Do not park on the right side of the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash means the action is not allowed. In this case, right turns are not permitted.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you?

options.text: Speed up to get out of the way.
Stop immediately and block their path.
Do everything you can to clear a path for them.
Signal to them when it is safe to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do everything you can to clear a path for them.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle has flashing lights, you must do everything possible to give them a clear path. If it is safe, pull to the side of the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians ahead.
End of construction zone.
School crossing ahead.
Flagger ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flagger ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a flagger is ahead. A flagger controls traffic in a construction area.

questions.question: How should you prepare for what might be coming up on the road ahead?

options.text: Look at the entire road and all roadsides constantly.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Drive with your left foot resting lightly on the brake pedal.
Keep your focus on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and all roadsides constantly.
questions.explanation: To handle dangerous situations, you must spot problems before you reach them. Scan the entire road, including the sides. Do not just stare at the center of the road.

questions.question: If you are in an accident and oncoming traffic cannot see the accident scene, what should you do?

options.text: Have someone warn approaching traffic.
Let oncoming traffic watch out for themselves.
Let the police handle everything.
Assume other drivers heard the crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have someone warn approaching traffic.
questions.explanation: Warn oncoming drivers to prevent more crashes. Have someone alert approaching traffic. Keep a flashlight and flares in your car for emergencies.

questions.question: When driving where children are playing, what should you expect?

options.text: They know when it is safe to cross the street.
They will stop at the curb before crossing.
They may run out in front of you without looking.
They will not cross unless an adult is with them.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may run out in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be extra careful around children. They may not understand the danger and could run in front of you without looking.

questions.question: Distracted drivers have a higher crash risk when using which of these?

options.text: CD player
Radio
Cell phone
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Cell phones (including hands-free phones) and audio devices (radios and CD players) are dangerous distractions. They increase your risk of crashing.

questions.question: Which statements about emergency vehicles are true?

options.text: They have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and/or flashing lights.
They may use a loudspeaker to give instructions.
They may follow each other.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Yield to police cars, fire engines, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using a siren or horn and flashing red or blue lights. Follow any instructions from their loudspeakers. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so only proceed when the way is clear.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, which of these should you do?

options.text: Look for turning vehicles before crossing a street.
Never run alongside or across a street.
Walk on the left side of the street, facing traffic.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not run alongside or across a street. Walk on the left side facing oncoming traffic. Always look for turning vehicles before crossing.

questions.question: What must you do when you see a red traffic light?

options.text: Stop at the stop line.
Stop before entering any crosswalk.
Stop before entering the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop before entering the intersection. Stop at the stop line and before entering any crosswalk.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at the same time at a four-way stop sign, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on the right.
The driver on the left.
One driver may continue driving without stopping.
One driver should honk to show they are giving up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, yield to the driver on your right if you both arrive at the same time. You may proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What happens when a driver goes much slower than the speed limit?

options.text: It is very safe driving.
They always have the right-of-way.
They should not let cars pass them.
It may create a dangerous driving environment.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may create a dangerous driving environment.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is hazardous. On two-lane roads, pull over and let traffic pass if cars are backing up behind you. Only drive significantly under the speed limit when conditions require it.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, what should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Wave your arms.
Use your emergency lights.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound your horn.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who might not see you. If you think another driver is about to hit you, sound your horn.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Rely only on your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to see if it is safe.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, always check behind your vehicle. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to look through the rear window while backing. Do not depend only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing with no gates or flashing lights, but with a crossbuck sign. You should:

options.text: Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you know no train is coming.
Turn your radio down to listen for an approaching train.
Only continue when a flagger clears you, if one is present.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always approach all railroad crossings with extreme caution. Cross only when you know no train is coming from either direction. If a flagger is present, follow their instructions.

questions.question: When driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and be prepared to stop.
Take the right-of-way.
Proceed normally.
Drive away quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be prepared to stop.
questions.explanation: When near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and give them the right-of-way. Be ready to stop to prevent injury or danger.

questions.question: You should drive below the posted speed limit when:

options.text: Anything makes conditions less than perfect.
You see a police car.
You are entering a highway with other cars.
You are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything makes conditions less than perfect.
questions.explanation: When roads are wet or slippery, when visibility is poor, or when conditions are not ideal, drive below the speed limit. Even if you are driving at the posted speed limit, you can be ticketed for driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed when roads are wet.
Keep your tires at the proper air pressure.
Replace tires with worn tread.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when your vehicle slides on a thin layer of water between the tires and the road. Low tire pressure and worn tread increase hydroplaning risk. Speeding also increases this risk.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is not true?

options.text: Winter is the hardest driving season.
Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid levels in winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
Snow tires are the best choice for winter driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or similar hazardous conditions. Winter is the hardest driving season and requires extra care. Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid levels regularly. Snow tires improve traction on slippery roads.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, you should:

options.text: Not proceed until the children wave to you.
Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
Accelerate quickly.
Turn on your emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus with its stop arm extended and lights flashing, watch for children walking along the road. Always drive carefully near children.

questions.question: If a police officer asks you to take a blood alcohol test, you:

options.text: Do not have to take it if you can prove you were not drinking.
Must take it or risk losing your license.
Do not have to take it if you did not violate any traffic rule.
Must take it or risk a fine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must take it or risk losing your license.
questions.explanation: When you drive, you agree to take a blood alcohol test if a police officer requests it. Refusing the test will result in losing your license for at least one year.

questions.question: A solid red arrow in a traffic signal:

options.text: Is never used as a traffic signal.
Means the same thing as a red circular traffic light.
Means you may turn in the direction the arrow points.
Means traffic in that direction must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Means the same thing as a red circular traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red circular traffic light. When an arrow is red, traffic in that lane must stop and cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.
